name: Emily
description: Emily runs a family-operated horticulture farm with her husband and three children. The farm depends heavily on reliable irrigation to maintain crop quality and protect permanent plantings. Changes in water availability can increase operating costs, disrupt production planning and place pressure on the family's main source of income.
goals: Maintain reliable access to water for crop production
Plan planting and production around expected water availability
Keep the family farm financially sustainable as the household's main source of income
concerns: Having to shift toward lower-water-use crops when allocations are uncertain
Securing enough water to protect permanent almond and citrus plantings during low-allocation periods

current.summary: The regulated-river plan sets allocation priorities and carryover rules for licence holders. General-security allocations are made after higher-priority requirements are met.
rules: Allocation priority depends on licence category; general-security water is allocated after higher-priority requirements.
Eligible general-security accounts can carry over up to 30% of entitlement, subject to a 100% account limit.
current.farmerImpact: If Emily holds a general-security entitlement, lower seasonal allocations could leave less water for irrigating almonds, citrus and vegetables. She may need to adjust irrigation schedules, prioritise crops or seek additional water where trading is available. Carryover may offer flexibility between seasons, subject to her entitlement and the rules.

name: Jamie Wilson
description: Jamie manages a orchard and vineyard. Permanent plantings need dependable irrigation even when commodity prices soften.

current.summary: Victorian water shares receive seasonal allocations based on water availability. High-reliability shares are allocated before low-reliability shares; this order does not guarantee a full allocation.
current.sourceTitle: Victoria DEECA — How water is managed
rules: Seasonal determinations use storage levels, expected inflows and system commitments; high-reliability shares are allocated before low-reliability shares.
In the Murray system, carryover above the entitlement volume may sit in a spillable account and can be written off if storages spill.
current.farmerImpact: Jamie’s almond orchard and vineyard need irrigation across seasons. If allocations are low, they may need to adjust irrigation plans or consider water purchases where available. Carryover can help shift water between seasons, but spillable-account water may not be available immediately and could be lost if storages spill.

name: Casey
description: Casey grows cotton and grain in the Condamine-Balonne region. Cotton production depends on irrigation, so seasonal water availability shapes planting and farm planning. Local grower and irrigation groups connect producers with industry information and resources.
goals: Inferred: plan crop production with irrigation and water access in mind.
Inferred: stay connected with local grower and irrigation networks.
concerns: Inferred: water access and groundwater protection may matter to local growers.
Inferred: seasonal water availability may affect irrigation planning.

current.summary: The plan’s rules vary by water source and supply arrangement. Scheme-supplied water follows the relevant operations manual; unsupplemented water and some groundwater follow the water management protocol.
current.sourceTitle: Queensland Government — Condamine and Balonne Water Plan area
rules: Announced limits can restrict how much water may be taken under some entitlements; supplemented scheme rules are set out in the scheme operations manual.
Trading and seasonal water assignments are subject to the rules for the relevant scheme, water source and entitlement.
current.farmerImpact: Casey’s cotton and grain planning depends on which water source and scheme apply to the farm. A change in announced limits or scheme operations could affect irrigation timing or the area planted. Casey may consider water trading or seasonal assignment where permitted; the relevant rules and availability vary by entitlement and scheme.

current.summary: South Australia allocates River Murray water under its Water Allocation Plan. Available water is determined after system needs, including conveyance losses and critical human water needs, are considered.
current.sourceTitle: SA Government — How River Murray water is allocated
rules: In dry years, South Australia may receive a third share of available River Murray water rather than its full Basin Agreement entitlement.
Eligible Class 3 high-security holders may apply for private carryover of up to 20% when the announced trigger is met; availability is decided each year.
current.farmerImpact: Morgan’s citrus, almond and grape plantings need irrigation through the growing season. Reduced allocations could mean prioritising essential irrigation, reviewing water purchases or adjusting farm expenditure. Private carryover may provide flexibility only when Morgan meets the eligibility rules and the annual trigger is met; it is unavailable in 2026–27.
